Here, we report the results of the largest open community challenge in Inferring BInding Specificities (IBIS), where participants all over the world were invited to construct binding specificity models from multi-assay experimental data for poorly studied human transcription factors. The submissions were rigorously tested against a rich held-out dataset. Benchmarking demonstrated a consistent advantage of properly designed deep learning models over traditional positional weight matrices and other machine learning methods. Yet, the positional weight matrices displayed a surprisingly strong performance out of the box, being only slightly behind the best deep learning models. A post-challenge assessment of a selection of other deep learning methods further solidified this finding. IBIS highlights the power of benchmarking in finding adequate DNA motif representations, emphasizes the pros and cons of various machine learning methods applied to DNA motif modeling, and establishes a rich dataset, benchmarking protocols, and computational framework for a fair cross-platform evaluation of future models of transcription factor binding motifs in DNA sequences.

items.title: Conversational diagnostic artificial intelligence in ambulatory primary care: a prospective feasibility study.

sections.objective: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based systems show promise for assisting primary care providers (PCPs) with patient care. We aimed to evaluate the safety and quality of clinical conversations of a patient-facing conversational AI system, which engaged in real-world urgent primary care appointments.
sections.methods: In this prospective, single-centre, single-arm feasibility study, English-speaking patients aged at least 18 years interacted with the Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer (AMIE) up to 5 days before a single-complaint urgent primary care appointment. Physician safety supervisors monitored all interactions and were trained to intervene on the basis of predefined safety criteria. AMIE transcripts and summaries were shared with PCPs before the visit. Primary outcomes were the number of supervised conversation safety stops, AMIE's conversation quality assessed by clinical evaluators, and patient and PCP experiences per surveys. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06911398).
sections.results: From April to November, 2025, 114 patients were enrolled with 98 completing both the AMIE interaction and the PCP appointment. Zero conversation safety stops were required on the basis of prespecified criteria. Safety supervisors noted one hallucination and added clinical information in five interactions. AMIE's conversations were rated favourably in 87-100% of cases (17 criteria) by clinical evaluators, and 48-96% (16 criteria) by patients. Patient attitudes towards AI improved after interacting with AMIE and remained elevated after the patient's visit with their physician. PCPs completed post-surveys in 60 of 98 cases, including 44 cases in which they reviewed the AMIE transcript before the visit. PCPs found AMIE helpful for visit preparation in 33 of 44 cases and reported that it might have changed their behaviour in 25 of 44 cases.
sections.conclusion: Although further research is needed, this study shows the initial feasibility of conversational AI in a real-world setting-assessed via conversation safety and quality, as well as user acceptance-and represents a crucial step towards clinical translation.

items.title: Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.

sections.objective: In hereditary angioedema, a rare bradykinin-mediated condition, oral on-demand treatments facilitating prompt administration and providing rapid, sustained relief and attack resolution remain scant. We investigated the efficacy and safety of deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks.
sections.methods: RAPIDe-3 was a phase 3, double-blind, 2 × 2 crossover trial in adolescent and adult participants (aged ≥12 to <18 years and aged ≥18 to ≤75 years, respectively) with hereditary angioedema, at 59 sites across 24 countries on six continents. Eligible participants had hereditary angioedema, including those with normal C1 inhibitor associated with a documented genetic variant, at least two attacks within the last 3 months before screening, and experience with effectively using conventional on-demand therapies for hereditary angioedema attacks. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two double-blind crossover sequences to treat two attacks with a 20 mg oral deucrictibant immediate-release capsule or placebo as either deucrictibant-placebo or placebo-deucrictibant, stratified by age and use of long-term prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was time to onset of symptom relief, defined as Patient Global Impression of Change rating of at least a little better. Safety was assessed in all participants who received any dose of study drug. RAPIDe-3 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06343779) and is complete.
sections.results: Between April 4, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, 149 people were assessed for eligibility, and 134 eligible participants (ten [7%] adolescents and 124 [93%] adults) were randomly allocated. 58 (43%) were male and 76 (57%) were female, and the median age was 38·0 years (IQR 27·0-50·0). 113 participants treated 201 attacks. The primary efficacy analysis included 88 participants with paired treated attacks. Of these, 47 (53%) participants were female and 41 (47%) were male, and 60 (68%), 16 (18%), 4 (5%), and 1 (1%) were White, Asian, Black, and American Indian or Alaska Native, respectively. Onset of symptom relief occurred significantly faster with deucrictibant than placebo, with median times of 1·28 h (95% CI 1·05 to 1·52) and more than 12 h (5·82 to >12), respectively (p<0·0001). Fatigue was the only adverse event reported more than once within 3 days post-treatment: a single event was reported by two participants, one of which was deemed unrelated to treatment. Across the study, no treatment-related adverse events were assessed as severe or serious, and no adverse events led to treatment discontinuation.
sections.conclusion: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration.

items.title: Seven principles for a critical transdisciplinary approach to planetary health.
items.abstract: The ecological, social, and health crises of the Anthropocene demand approaches to knowledge that confront complexity, uncertainty, and structural injustice. Transdisciplinarity is an approach that can transcend disciplinary silos by integrating academic and non-academic knowledge. Yet, action on public health, planetary health, and health inequities is often implemented in technocratic, depoliticised, and tokenistic ways. Such practices risk marginalising lived experience, reinforcing epistemic hierarchies, and overlooking structural drivers such as capitalism, colonialism, and patriarchy. Drawing on examples from the exposome, One Health, and planetary health paradigms, we argue that current applications of transdisciplinarity privilege biomedical or technical framings, underplay systemic power relations, and fail to deliver transformative impact. A critical transdisciplinary approach is needed-one that is political, reflexive, justice oriented, and grounded in collaboration with affected communities, social movements, and practitioners. It should integrate diverse knowledge systems, value experiential and Indigenous perspectives, and align research with agendas for structural change. We propose seven guiding principles. The approach should be: critical, systemic, structural, sociohistorical, democratic, timely, and transformative. Advancing planetary health equity requires more than an understanding of the systemic determinants of disease and environmental degradation-it requires dismantling the political, economic, and cultural systems that perpetuate them. A critical transdisciplinary approach that follows these principles can guide research, policy, and practice, positioning knowledge not only as a tool for explanation but also as an instrument for transformation.

items.title: When the fungus is susceptible, but the patient is not: reading antifungal susceptibility from bench to bedside.
items.abstract: Antifungal susceptibility testing is increasingly available and is central to the management of invasive, refractory, recurrent, and breakthrough fungal infections. However, minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) are not self-interpreting results. They measure in vitro antifungal activity under defined laboratory conditions, but clinical outcome is shaped by species identification, method, breakpoint or epidemiological cutoff values, availability, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic exposure, infection site, fungal burden, source control, biofilm formation, and host immunity. Non-classic fungal drug-response phenotypes, including tolerance, heteroresistance, persistence, adaptive resistance, trailing growth, paradoxical growth, and biofilm-associated survival, can further weaken the link between a susceptible MIC and therapeutic success. In this Personal View, we argue that antifungal susceptibility testing should be understood as a shared clinical-laboratory interface rather than as a standalone laboratory result. The microbiologist makes the MIC interpretable by defining organism, method, interpretive threshold, confidence, and need for confirmation; the clinician makes it clinically useful by integrating exposure, site, source control, toxicity, interactions, and clinical trajectory. Future reports should therefore move from isolated MICs towards structured interpretation, uncertainty flags, and interpretive guidance, while avoiding forced susceptible-resistant categorisation when evidence is incomplete. Such reporting can strengthen stewardship, surveillance, and patient-level decisions across tertiary, routine, and resource-constrained settings, without overstating what MICs can predict alone at the bedside.

items.title: Quantitative Proteomics of Plasma-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Reveals a Plasminogen-Centered Protein Network in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.

sections.objective: The prognosis of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR) remains poor; this is primarily due to late diagnosis, when irreversible damage has already occurred. Circulating levels of transthyretin or other plasma markers have little value for diagnosis. Although extracellular vesicles (EVs) (key mediators of intercellular communication) may reflect disease-specific molecular changes, their protein cargo has not yet been explored in the context of ATTR cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). We evaluated whether cardiac amyloidosis alters the proteome of circulating EVs and assessed whether these changes define signature of ATTR.
sections.methods: Plasma EVs were prospectively isolated by ultracentrifugation from 41 patients with confirmed ATTR-CM (ATTR+ group; wild-type ATTR and variant ATTR) and 24 frequency-matched patients with nonamyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR- group), all referred to the Referral Center for Cardiac Amyloidosis (Henri Mondor Hospital, Créteil, France). EVs were characterized by flow cytometry and analyzed by quantitative liquid chromatography mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry proteomics.
sections.results: ATTR+ patients had a distinct signature enriched in proteins associated with vascular homeostasis, coagulation, and inflammation. At least 18 of these proteins formed an interconnected network centered on plasmin/plasminogen. Notably, EV levels of transthyretin and plasminogen were elevated, whereas the level of alpha2-antiplasmin (plasmin's primary inhibitor) was low. This imbalance is particularly relevant because plasmin is known to promote amyloidogenesis via transthyretin cleavage.
sections.conclusion: These exploratory findings highlight a plasmin/plasminogen-centered protein network linking fibrinolysis, complement activation, and vascular inflammation to ATTR pathophysiology, and suggest that plasma EV proteomics warrant further evaluation as a minimally invasive approach for disease monitoring and biomarker discovery in ATTR-CM.

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Course Prediction in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Using Baseline OCT from a Multicenter Cohort.

sections.objective: To predict disease clinical course in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) using an interpretable machine learning model applied to baseline artificial intelligence (AI)-derived optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers acquired at first presentation.
sections.methods: Multicenter, retrospective cohort study. Overall, 329 treatment-naïve CSC eyes recruited across eight international centers in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and North Africa. Treatment-naïve CSC patients were retrospectively included and classified, based on follow-up, as acute or chronic CSC according to subretinal fluid (SRF) resolution. Baseline OCT biomarkers were extracted using an AI-based platform (Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector; RetinAI AG, Switzerland), which quantified retinal layer thicknesses, including the outer nuclear layer (ONL) and photoreceptor-retinal pigment epithelium (PR+RPE) complex, fluid volumes (SRF and RPE detachment [PED]), and biomarker probabilities, across central, parafoveal, and perifoveal ETDRS regions. These features used to develop an interpretable machine learning model predicting future CSC chronicity. Classification of eyes as acute or chronic CSC, determined by SRF resolution on follow-up; discriminative performance of the Random Forest classifier, assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); and biomarker importance, evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values.
sections.results: Of 329 eyes (291 patients), 92 (28.0%) were classified as acute and 237 (72.0%) as chronic CSC; mean follow-up was 4.2 ± 1.6 years. Chronic CSC patients were significantly older (51.7 ± 12.6 vs. 43.2 ± 9.6 years, p<0.001) with worse baseline visual acuity (0.25 ± 0.21 vs. 0.16 ± 0.15 logMAR, p=0.029). Among baseline OCT biomarkers, parafoveal ONL thickness showed the strongest association with disease chronicity (q<0.0001; r=-0.414). The Random Forest classifier achieved an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.748-0.940). SHAP analysis identified parafoveal ONL thickness, perifoveal PR+RPE thickness, and central SRF volume as the strongest predictors of acute CSC, whereas greater RNFL thickness, PED volume, FLAT PED probability, and HF probability were the most influential predictors of chronic disease.
sections.conclusion: Automatically detected OCT biomarkers can predict CSC chronicity at initial presentation with good discriminatory performance. Quantitative markers of outer retinal integrity, fluid configuration, and RPE dysfunction may improve prognostication, facilitate patient counseling, and help identify individuals at increased risk of persistent CSC.

items.title: Technology-Supported Solutions to Improve Guideline-Informed Care for Kidney Disease: Conclusions from a Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference.
items.abstract: Implementation of guideline-informed care for the prevention, detection, and management of kidney disease remains suboptimal throughout the world. In November 2025, Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) held a Controversies Conference on the role of technology-supported solutions to improve guideline-informed care for people with or at risk for kidney disease and to identify priorities for research. There have been rapid advances in various technologies for earlier identification of people with kidney disease; risk stratification for adverse kidney, cardiovascular, and other clinical and patient-centered outcomes; and promotion of guideline-informed therapies, monitoring, and patient self-management. Still, there remain important considerations for how to optimize the use of such technologies for achieving care that is integrated, personalized, safe, and guideline-informed. The conference identified a range of lived experience, clinician, health care system, health policy, and technology-level factors that can influence the effectiveness of technology-supported solutions in improving guideline-informed care. Research priorities included developing and maintaining living guidelines; harmonizing and integrating guideline recommendations into clinical decision support solutions; generating evidence on the effectiveness and safety of technology-supported solutions that reduce disparities and preserve trust; developing and evaluating efforts that promote interoperability, feasibility and scalability of technologies across health care systems; developing more effective public-private partnerships and systematic use of validated health technology assessments; and clarifying the incremental value of emerging technologies involving sensor-derived biomarkers and integrated multimodal data. Strategies to optimize digital health technologies for promoting guideline-informed care were also delineated.

items.title: Comparison of efficacy and tolerability of hedgehog pathway inhibitors for locally advanced basal cell carcinoma: An expert opinion in the new age of immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most diagnosed malignancy. While most cases are curable, a subset progresses to unresectable locally advanced (laBCC) or metastatic BCC (mBCC). The Smoothened inhibitors (SMOi) vismodegib and sonidegib have significantly improved outcomes in these cases. However, differences in trial design, pharmacokinetics, adverse effects (AEs), and real-world application warrant clinical comparison. This narrative review examines key clinical trials (ERIVANCE, BOLT, STEVIE, MIKIE), FDA labeling, and real-world data. Efficacy outcomes, AE profiles, pharmacokinetics, and resistance mechanisms are analyzed alongside expert recommendations for optimizing treatment. In expert opinion, sonidegib demonstrates a longer median duration of response and more durable disease control compared to vismodegib. Its delayed-onset AEs and deeper tissue penetration make it favorable for infiltrative or high-risk disease. Vismodegib, though more widely prescribed, is associated with earlier-onset AEs and challenges with treatment interruptions due to its shorter half-life. Tailored dosing and AE mitigation strategies as well as neoadjuvant applications of SMOi improve tolerability and outcomes for both agents. Both vismodegib and sonidegib remain essential tools in the management of advanced BCC. Understanding their pharmacologic and clinical differences enables more personalized treatment planning, enhancing long-term outcomes and expanding their use in neoadjuvant and maintenance settings.

items.title: Acquired Hair Texture Alteration After Regrowth in Alopecia Areata: A Distinct Clinical and Ultrastructural Phenotype.

sections.objective: Post-regrowth hair texture alteration between straight and curly or kinked hair is rare and poorly understood in alopecia areata (AA). To characterize clinical and ultrastructural features of this phenomenon.
sections.methods: A retrospective multicenter case-control study of AA patients and a systematic literature review were performed. Clinical, dermoscopic, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) findings were analyzed.
sections.results: Twenty-nine cases and 145 controls were enrolled. Univariable analysis showed hair texture alteration was more frequent in females and those with severe-to-very-severe diffuse AA or totalis/universalis. Most hair texture alterations occurred 4-12 weeks following Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors and/or systemic steroid therapy, or following spontaneous hair regrowth. SEM revealed acquired pili torti, characterized by flattened hair shafts, segmental longitudinal grooves, and 180° axial twisting. The literature review identified five additional cases, expanding the therapeutic spectrum to topical/intralesional glucocorticoids and diphenylcyclopropenone (DPCP). In our series, 17.2% (5/29) of patients reverted to their original straight texture after 7 (7.0, 12.5) months, while others remained curly at a median follow-up of 12 (6.0, 18.0) months. Limitations Retrospective design.
sections.conclusion: Hair texture alteration after AA regrowth represents a distinct, underrecognized phenotype, likely reflecting intrinsic hair shaft abnormalities during follicular recovery rather than treatment effects.

items.title: Sofetabart mipitecan, an antibody drug conjugate targeting folate receptor alpha, in high grade ovarian cancer: Results from the first-in-human phase 1 study.

sections.objective: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) is overexpressed in most high-grade ovarian cancers (HGOC), but use of the FRα-targeting drug mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx (MIRV) is limited by expression-level restrictions and toxicity profile. Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) is a novel FRα-targeting antibody-drug conjugate designed to overcome these barriers. Here we report safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics from the first-in-human phase 1 study.
sections.methods: This multicenter, open-label, phase 1 trial evaluated Sofe-M in patients with HGOC, regardless of FRα expression level. Prior MIRV treatment was permitted.
sections.results: One-hundred-five patients with HGOC, the majority of whom were platinum resistant, received Sofe-M at 2, 3, 4 or 6 mg/kg every 21 days. Median age was 63.0 years, median number of prior treatments was 5.0 (1-11), 19 (18.1%) patients had prior MIRV, and 54 (51.4%) had tumor FRα expression <75% at ≥2+ intensity. Overall response rate was 50.5% (95% CI 40.5, 60.4) for all patients, 58.8% (95% CI 32.9, 81.6) at 3 mg/kg, 44.4% (95% CI 30.9, 58.6) for FRα <75%, 56.5% (95% CI, 41.1, 71.1) for FRα ≥75%, and 57.9% (95% CI 33.5, 79.7) for patients with prior MIRV exposure. Median progression-free survival was 8.1 months (95% CI 6.4, 8.5) and median follow-up was 12.9 months (95% CI 10.6, 15.2). Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were nausea (64.8%), fatigue (56.2%), and anemia (47.6%). No keratopathies or grade ≥3 neuropathy were observed. At 3 and 4 mg/kg, the rate of Grade ≥3 treatment-related TEAEs was 35.3% and 56.4%, respectively. Treatment discontinuation due to TEAEs occurred in 11 patients (10.5%).
sections.conclusion: Sofe-M demonstrated a favorable tolerability profile, notably absent of keratopathy and high-grade neuropathy, with durable clinical activity in heavily pretreated HGOC patients regardless of FRα expression level or prior MIRV. These data support 3 mg/kg as the recommended phase 3 dose and provide the basis for the FRAmework-01 trial.

items.title: Postural Intraocular Pressure Changes and the Trans-Lamina Cribrosa Pressure Difference: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42024556443) addresses the magnitude of intraocular pressure (IOP) changes when transitioning from sitting to supine and lateral decubitus positions. It investigates the interaction with intracranial pressure (ICP) to estimate the translaminar cribrosa pressure difference (TLPD). Participants included healthy individuals, glaucoma suspects, and patients with ocular hypertension or glaucoma.
sections.methods: We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Embase from inception to July 2024 for observational and interventional studies measuring IOP or ICP in at least two body positions. Eligibility criteria required quantitative reporting in mmHg; studies confounding posture with circadian rhythm were excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions for observational studies and the Risk of Bias 2.0 tool for the randomized trial.
sections.results: Thirty-two cohorts comprising 2,842 eyes and 2,385 patients (weighted mean age 61.5 years) were included; 27 studies contributed quantitative data, including 22 for the supine-versus-sitting analysis. Supine IOP increases were +2.49 mmHg (95% CI, 1.33-3.65) in healthy eyes, +2.89 mmHg (95% CI, 2.27-3.50) in the glaucoma spectrum, and +3.60 mmHg (95% CI, 3.24-3.96) in ocular hypertension (one study). The dependent lateral decubitus eye increased by +3.92 mmHg (95% CI, 3.08-4.75). Qualitative synthesis suggested lower ICP in several glaucoma cohorts, although most IOP and ICP measurements were asynchronous.
sections.conclusion: Glaucoma management relies on IOP measurements taken upright during clinic hours. This paradigm overlooks nocturnal stressors occurring during recumbency, which occupies one-third of a patient's life. Postural IOP elevations, particularly when coupled with low ICP, may drive disease progression in patients who appear stable during diurnal visits, especially those with normal-tension glaucoma (NTG). Recumbency induces significant IOP elevations, pronounced in the dependent eye during lateral decubitus positioning. Current evidence hypothesizes a potential double hit for patients with NTG who may lack cerebrospinal fluid counter-pressure, though this relies largely on inferred, asynchronous measurements. While limited by heterogeneity and reliance on ICP estimates, these findings highlight the necessity of future longitudinal research into nocturnal postural physiology to determine its role in glaucoma management.

items.title: Association Between Leg Venous Reflux and Fluid Accumulation Assessed by Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis: A Generalized Estimating Equation Analysis.

sections.objective: Leg edema is common in chronic venous disease, but its relationship with venous reflux remains unclear. This study investigated the association between the venous filling index (VFI) and the extracellular water-to-total body water ratio (ECW/TBW).
sections.methods: We analyzed 140 patients with saphenous varicose veins (280 limbs). ECW/TBW was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis and VFI using air plethysmography. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to account for within-patient correlation. The primary outcome was ECW/TBW (%) analyzed using GEE linear regression, and the secondary outcome was edema (ECW/TBW ≥0.390) analyzed using GEE logistic regression.
sections.results: The mean age was 64.0 years, and 58.6% of patients were female. Mean ECW/TBW was 0.392 and mean VFI was 2.94 mL/s. In multivariable GEE linear regression, VFI was independently associated with higher ECW/TBW (%) (β=0.045 percentage points per 1 mL/s increase; 95% CI, 0.018-0.072; P<0.001). In multivariable GEE logistic regression, VFI was independently associated with edema (OR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.22-1.76; P<0.001).
sections.conclusion: Greater venous reflux was independently associated with fluid accumulation and edema. ECW/TBW may provide an objective measure of venous-related fluid accumulation.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of artificial intelligence-assisted image-guided navigation in complex endovascular aortic repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Complex endovascular aortic repair exposes patients and operators to substantial radiation, contrast, and long procedures. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image-guided navigation, based on cloud-based three-dimensional image fusion, has been proposed to improve intraoperative guidance, but its comparative benefit is uncertain.
sections.methods: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (last search July 2025) for studies comparing AI-assisted image-guided navigation with conventional fluoroscopy and digital subtraction angiography during complex endovascular aortic repair. No navigation platform was prespecified. Random-effects meta-analyses yielded mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was quantified with I 2 . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and certainty with GRADE.
sections.results: Three retrospective cohorts (332 patients; 189 AI, 143 control), all evaluating one cloud-based platform (Cydar EV), were eligible. AI-assisted navigation was associated with a lower radiation dose (2 studies, 216 patients; MD -1435.85 mGy, 95% CI -2208.84 to -662.86; I 2 = 0%). No significant differences were found in fluoroscopy time (MD -11.04 minutes, 95% CI -25.37 to 3.29; I 2 = 65%), operative time (MD -16.39 minutes, 95% CI -37.21 to 4.42; I 2 = 0%), or contrast volume (MD -30.59 mL, 95% CI -73.95 to 12.76; I 2 = 94%). Mortality and major adverse events (single studies) did not differ significantly.
sections.conclusion: Cydar EV-assisted navigation may reduce radiation dose during complex endovascular aortic repair, but evidence is limited to retrospective studies of a single platform and does not establish a class effect for other AI-assisted navigation systems. Prospective comparative studies across platforms are needed.

items.title: Histone Demethylase KDM5A Is Activated and Pathogenic in a Mouse Model of LMNA-Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Heart failure is associated with widespread epigenetic remodeling in cardiomyocytes, but the chromatin regulators driving this process remain poorly defined. We identify the histone H3K4 demethylase KDM5A as a key epigenetic mediator of heart failure in a cardiomyocyte-specific lamin A-deficient mouse model. Disease-associated activation of KDM5A leads to redistribution of promoter histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation and repression of genes regulating sarcomere structure and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Genetic deletion of Kdm5a restores histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation enrichment, reactivates cardiac and metabolic transcriptional programs, improves cardiac function, and prolongs survival. These findings identify KDM5A-mediated chromatin remodeling as a previously unrecognized mechanism of heart failure and highlight KDM5A as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism in Pregnancy: A Case Report and a Systematic Review of the Literature.
items.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) in pregnancy is a major clinical challenge with potentially fatal maternal and fetal outcomes. Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) offers a promising alternative when thrombolysis is contraindicated, although evidence in pregnancy is limited. We describe a 26-year-old at 29 + 5 weeks' gestation with high-risk PE causing acute right heart failure, successfully treated, achieving rapid hemodynamic recovery, and minimal fetal radiation exposure. A systematic review identified 15 MT cases in pregnancy or peripartum (11 antepartum, 4 postpartum), reporting 100% maternal survival and favorable fetal outcomes in 87% (1 fetal death, 1 abortion). Complications occurred in 40%, including hemolysis, renal failure, and hemorrhagic shock. MT appears to be an effective, potentially life-saving option in selected obstetric patients when performed in experienced centers with multidisciplinary support.Clinical ImpactMechanical thrombectomy (MT) represents a valuable therapeutic option for high-risk pulmonary embolism in pregnancy when thrombolysis is contraindicated. In this setting, MT allows for rapid reperfusion and hemodynamic stabilization while avoiding the bleeding risks associated with systemic fibrinolysis. Early consideration of MT within a multidisciplinary framework might significantly improve maternal prognosis without compromising fetal safety.

items.title: Stent-Graft Fracture 18 Years After Hybrid Repair of Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Possible Risk of Retrograde Reconstruction.
items.abstract: We report the case of a patient who underwent hybrid repair for a type V thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. The procedure ensured durable aneurysm exclusion and visceral perfusion for 18 years. Eighteen years after surgery, the stent-graft fractured occurred at the visceral artery segment. Fluid-structure interaction analysis revealed a progressive elevation of von Mises stress at the eventual fracture site. Compared with in situ reconstruction, retrograde reconstruction in hybrid repair may increase the risk of stent-related complications. Monitoring von Mises stress during follow-up may help predict fracture and allow early intervention.Clinical ImpactLate stent-graft fracture after hybrid repair can occur despite effective aneurysm exclusion and satisfactory visceral perfusion. This case highlights the importance of long-term surveillance of graft integrity and changes in aortic morphology. A gradual increase in tortuosity and progressive elongation of the aorta may warrant particular attention, even many years after surgery. Fluid-structure interaction analysis linked progressive elevation of von Mises stress to the eventual fracture site and suggested that retrograde reconstruction may increase localized stress compared with in situ reconstruction. Integrating longitudinal imaging with patient-specific stress analysis may help clinicians recognize graft segments that warrant closer follow-up.

items.title: Early Outcomes of Physician-Modified Endurant Limbs vs Iliac Branch Devices in Narrow Common Iliac Arteries: A Retrospective Cohort Pilot Study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the feasibility and short-term outcomes of physician-modified Endurant limbs (PMEGs) for internal iliac artery (IIA) preservation in patients with narrow common iliac artery (CIA) anatomy, with descriptive comparison to commercially available iliac branch devices (IBDs).
sections.methods: This retrospective multicenter pilot study included 20 consecutive patients with a CIA bifurcation diameter ≤18 mm who underwent endovascular aneurysm repair with preservation of at least 1IIA between January 2023 and December 2025. Ten patients were treated with PMEG and 10 with commercially available IBDs. Primary outcomes were technical success and IIA branch patency. Secondary outcomes included operative time, back-table modification time, endoleaks, reinterventions, and perioperative outcomes.
sections.results: Technical success was achieved in all patients. Internal iliac artery branch patency was 100% at 1 and 3 months in both groups and remained 100% in the PMEG group vs 90% in the IBD group at 12 months. No type I/III endoleaks or iliac-related reinterventions occurred. Operative time was similar between groups, while mean PMEG modification time was 61.5 ± 26.4 minutes. No modification-related complications or procedure-related mortality occurred.
sections.conclusion: The PMEG appears to be a feasible option for IIA preservation in patients with narrow iliac anatomy, demonstrating favorable early outcomes. Given the pilot design, small sample size, and limited follow-up, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger prospective studies.Clinical ImpactPMEGs may be a feasible option for IIA preservation in patients with narrow CIA anatomy when standard IBDs are limited by profile or availability. This approach may expand endovascular options in selected cases, emphasizing careful planning and technical flexibility. Given the small sample size, these findings warrant cautious interpretation and validation in larger studies.

items.title: Low-Profile Versus Standard-Profile Endograft for Thoracoabdominal and Complex Abdominal Endovascular Aortic Treatment-Multicenter Cohort Study.

sections.objective: The introduction of low-profile stent grafts (LPSGs) has proven to be a useful option despite initial concerns. The aim of this study was to analyze and compare the outcomes of standard-profile stent grafts (SPSGs) versus LPSG in a cohort of patients treated for thoracoabdominal (TAAA) and complex abdominal (CAAA) aortic aneurysms.
sections.methods: A multi-center cohort study based on a retrospective analysis of consecutive patients admitted for the treatment of TAAA and CAAA using fenestrated and/or branched endovascular aneurysm repair (FB-EVAR) was performed. Outcomes were compared in patients treated with LPSG versus SPSG including procedural metrics, technical success (TS), clinical complications, access-related complications, overall survival, stent-graft integrity issues, secondary interventions, sac enlargement, and primary patency of target vessels (TVs).
sections.results: A total of 478 patients were included, with a mean age of 71.6 years (±8.96), and 80.3% were male. There were 227 TAAAs and 251 CAAAs, with a median of 4 (interquartile range [IQR]: 4-4) vessels catheterized per patient. Low-profile stent grafts were used in 137 (28.7%) patients and SPSGs in 341 (71.3%) patients. Low-profile stent grafts were more frequently used in patients with previous aortic surgery (44.9% vs 33.6%, P = .022), and the number of TVs treated differed significantly between LPSG and SPSG (4, IQR: 4-4 vs 4, IQR: 3-4; P P = .006). The tortuosity index was also higher in the LPSG group (1.35 ± 0.23) compared with in the SPSG group (1.29 ± 0.16, P = .030). Patients treated with LPSG had a similar TS rate (92.7% vs 95.0%, P = .33). There were no significant differences in postoperative complications. The median follow-up period was 6.9 months (IQR: 0.8-28.7). Regarding persistent or late endoleaks, no statistically significant differences were observed ( P = .36). Overall survival (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.06; 95% CI, 0.66-1.71; P = .78) and freedom from reintervention (HR: 1.04; 95% CI, 0.64-1.70; P = .86) were also similar between groups.
sections.conclusion: Fenestrated and/or branched endovascular aneurysm repair with LPSG and SPSG was performed with similar rates of TS and mortality. Low-profile stent grafts were more often used in complex cases with prior aortic repairs and challenging access. Early and mid-term outcomes were comparable, with both devices showing similar safety and effectiveness profiles.Clinical ImpactWe performed a retrospective, multicenter cohort study including 478 patients, comparing low-profile stent grafts with standard-profile grafts in the treatment of complex aortic aneurysms. Both types of stent grafts demonstrated similar technical success, safety, and effectiveness. Low-profile endografts proved to be a viable option, particularly in more challenging cases.

items.title: Circulating Metalloproteinase Inhibitors and Artificial Intelligence-Derived Radiomics Predict Persistent Endoleak After Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Multimodal Biological-Imaging Model.

sections.objective: Persistent endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) reflects ongoing aneurysm sac biological activity and remains insufficiently predicted by anatomical surveillance alone. We aimed to evaluate whether integration of circulating matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), and artificial intelligence (AI)-derived radiomic features from computed tomographic angiography (CTA) improves prediction of persistent endoleak.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study including 62 consecutive patients undergoing elective infrarenal EVAR between January 2020 and December 2024. Plasma levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-10, TIMP-1, and TIMP-2 were measured preoperatively and at 1 and 12 months post-EVAR. Computed tomography angiography data sets were analyzed using a standardized semi-automated radiomics pipeline with reproducibility testing and penalized feature selection. The primary endpoint was persistent endoleak at 12 months. Multivariable logistic regression was constructed with event-per-variable control and internally validated using bootstrap resampling.
sections.results: Persistent endoleak occurred in 18 patients (29%). Patients with persistent endoleak exhibited significantly higher MMP-9 levels, lower TIMP-1 and TIMP-2 levels, and markedly elevated MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratios at 1 month (all P < .01). Radiomics demonstrated increased intraluminal thrombus (ILT) entropy and reduced ILT density in the endoleak group. A parsimonious model including MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio and ILT entropy yielded an optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) of 0.81 with good calibration, outperforming sac diameter change alone (AUC = 0.62).
sections.conclusion: Persistent endoleak is associated with systemic proteolytic imbalance and imaging-detectable thrombus heterogeneity. Integration of biological and radiomic markers improves risk stratification compared with morphological surveillance alone and warrants prospective validation.Clinical ImpactThis study proposes a novel multimodal approach to post-EVAR surveillance by integrating circulating metalloproteinase inhibitors with AI-derived CT radiomics. Combining biological biomarkers with quantitative analysis of peri-EVAR thrombus volume and density may improve identification of patients at risk of persistent endoleak beyond conventional imaging assessment. For clinicians, this approach could enable earlier risk stratification, support personalised surveillance intervals, and identify patients who may benefit from closer imaging follow-up or intervention. The innovation lies in integrating systemic biological activity with local imaging phenotypes within a predictive model, moving EVAR surveillance from a predominantly anatomical strategy towards a personalised, data-driven biological-imaging paradigm.

items.title: Alzheimer's disease target and drug discovery by leveraging multiomics and electronic health data.
items.abstract: Despite prolific genomic data from individuals with Alzheimer's disease (AD), translation into treatments has lagged. Here we applied Mendelian randomization to multiple AD genome-wide association studies and functional multiomics datasets to nominate druggable targets, identifying 19 targets for individuals of European ancestry and 7 for African ancestry. This included epoxide hydrolase 2 (EPHX2), for which we identified a protective missense variant (p.Arg287Gln). Experiments in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons and cerebral organoids from patients with AD validated the protective role of p.Arg287Gln via reduced levels of EPHX2 and phosphorylated tau (pTau-181). Pharmacological inhibition of EPHX2 improved cognitive performance in the 5xFAD mouse model of AD. Finally, by leveraging electronic health data from 111,680 patients with mild cognitive impairment, we identified 12 drugs associated with reduced AD incidence, including trazodone (targeting ADRA1A) and baclofen (targeting GABBR1). Thus, integrating multiomics data, functional validation and electronic health data identifies new approaches for treating AD.

items.title: Simultaneous awake replay of multiple spatial representations.
items.abstract: How the hippocampus processes multiple spatial memories during awake decision-making remains unclear. Using a rat observational navigation task, we tested whether distinct spatial representations are replayed simultaneously during sharp-wave ripple-associated population bursts. Place cell sequences representing multiple T-maze trajectories were frequently replayed together during reward consumption and were particularly prominent in the observation box. These simultaneous replay events reflected the spatial organization of the maze, preferentially converged on reward sites, distinguished future behavioral choices, and were associated with choice-selective activity in anterior cingulate cortex. Replay of a single trajectory showed weaker relationships to behavior and cortical activity. These findings establish simultaneous awake replay of multiple spatial representations and support a role for parallel hippocampal processing during reward-directed observational navigation.

items.title: Comprehensive lineage tracing maps the landscape of cell fate decisions in mouse embryogenesis.
items.abstract: A comprehensive cell fate map of mammalian embryogenesis has remained out of reach given the scale, cellular diversity, and non-deterministic nature of development in utero. Here, we use PEtracer to continuously install heritable genetic marks as development progresses, reconstructing lineage trees that resolve ∼75% of cell divisions across >1.4 million cells from 16 replicate embryos. We pair these trees with deep transcriptional profiling to resolve cell fate biases, restriction timing, progenitor pool sizes, and lineage relationships throughout embryogenesis. Using this quantitative reference, we uncover strikingly reproducible lineage architecture between replicate embryos and chart the lineage dynamics driving fate specification across diverse tissues. Specific biological insights include the progressive restriction of neural crest fate, the relative contributions of distinct mesodermal origins to endothelium, and the dynamics of axial elongation. This work provides a foundation for a quantitative and predictive understanding of mammalian development.

items.title: Immunoregulatory gene GIMAP6 suppresses lethal atherosclerotic vasculopathy and ischemic heart failure.
items.abstract: Controlling hyperlipidemia has reduced but not eliminated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) as a major cause of human mortality. Here, we report that loss of the immunoregulatory gene GTPase of immunity-associated protein 6 (Gimap6) in mice causes an inflammatory vasculopathy and accelerated atherosclerosis in the absence of hyperlipidemia. These vascular abnormalities cause progressive cardiac ischemia, myocardial infarction, and heart failure, culminating in early death. GIMAP6 loss precipitates early endothelial barrier failure and a mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS)-PPARγ-CD36 lipid-influx cascade that lowers the threshold for foam-cell formation and induces IL-6/MCP-1/TNF-mediated inflammation. Human hypomorphic GIMAP6 variants, including the African-ancestry-enriched V65I allele, are associated with altered monocyte redox balance, increased CD36-mediated lipid uptake, and early ASCVD. Thus, GIMAP6 is a crucial safeguard for vascular integrity that restrains endothelial dysfunction, macrophage foam cell generation, and inflammation that can cause lethal ASCVD independently of systemic hyperlipidemia.

items.title: Native pathogen-phage networks reveal multilayered defense and gut-active anti-phage immunity.
items.abstract: Bacteriophages drive pathogen evolution, yet the mechanisms governing phage susceptibility in native bacterial backgrounds, and their consequences within mammalian hosts, remain poorly understood. Here, we mapped >1,000 interactions between 20 diverse Salmonella isolates and 52 wild phages from global disease reservoirs, integrating genome-scale fitness profiling with comparative genomics. Receptor identity and surface phase variation, including Hin-mediated flagellar switching, explained ∼67% of phage susceptibility patterns, identifying cell-surface architecture as the major determinant of phage host range in Salmonella. Among resistance phenotypes not explained by surface features, we discovered anti-phage-packaging agent (AppA), a prophage-encoded defense factor that abrogates phage replication within its native host. AppA inhibits phage DNA packaging through functional mimicry of a terminase assembly interface, revealing a previously unrecognized mechanism of phage defense. AppA is expressed under conditions encountered during mammalian infection and suppresses phage expansion in the murine gut, demonstrating that prophage-encoded single-gene defenses can shape disease outcomes in vivo.

items.title: A fluctuation test for gastruloid heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Stem cells self-organize into models of early development, but even under carefully controlled conditions, the resulting organoids exhibit substantial "inter-individual" heterogeneity. To explore its origins, we generated monoclonal gastruloids, each derived from a single mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC). Molecular profiling revealed extensive heterogeneity: some gastruloids failed to develop, others were biased toward mesodermal or neural fates, and yet others contained cell types atypical of conventional polyclonal gastruloids. Applying DNA Typewriter, a cell lineage recorder, we identified heritable fate biases arising prior to gastruloid induction and found that more closely related founder mESCs give rise to more phenotypically similar gastruloids. Linking mESC subclones to their descendants' fates revealed cryptic, fate-predictive differences in gene expression and chromatin accessibility, including at imprinted, methylation-sensitive loci linked to developmental potency. Intrinsic, heritable fluctuations in mESC state are therefore an important source of organoid heterogeneity, and DNA Typewriter enables high-resolution lineage trees in stem cell models.

items.title: Arabidopsis uses distinct coumarins and bacterial pathways for pH-adaptive iron acquisition.
items.abstract: Iron (Fe) limitation restricts plant growth in diverse soils, and root-associated microbes can alleviate plant Fe starvation. Whether plants integrate the edaphic environment and microbial activities into their Fe uptake strategies remains unclear. We show that bacterium-mediated alleviation of Fe deficiency in Arabidopsis functions at varying environmental pH and is taxonomically widespread among root microbiota isolates from soils with different edaphic profiles. This process is regulated by host-controlled and pH-adapted root exudation of different coumarin chemotypes. These exometabolites interact with root-associated bacteria to mobilize Fe either via bacterial siderophore-mediated chelation at circumneutral pH or redox-sensing-controlled, reduction-based pathways at acidic pH. The corresponding bacterial genes are prevalent in the root microbiota, and they likely evolved before the emergence of land plants. Our findings suggest that Fe malnutrition-induced exudation of redox-active metabolites by non-graminaceous plant species is a widespread adaptation for Fe mobilization from soil, mediated by the co-option of ancient microbial processes.

items.title: Nutritional interventions' impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings.
items.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B-vitamins, while macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

items.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth.
items.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multi-omics - metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides - across 1,543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multi-omic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas-informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune/repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

items.title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea-level rise.
items.abstract: Sea-level rise (SLR) threatens terrestrial biodiversity, yet its spatiotemporal and species-specific impacts remain unclear. Integrating relative SLR projections across five Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) with Area of Habitat (AOH) maps for 34,120 terrestrial vertebrate species, we project species exposed to SLR will increase from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57-63% of birds, 47-52% of mammals, 28-36% of reptiles, and 20-24% of amphibians. In Southeast Asia, inland inundation areas support high richness. Under SSP5-8.5, species facing >10% habitat inundation surges from 18 in 2050 to 109 by 2100, with reptiles and already threatened species overrepresented. Safeguarding SLR refugia, the non-inundated habitats for exposed species, is critical, yet over 96% lie outside protected areas, demanding early international action.

items.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang.
items.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over approximately 80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

items.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis.
items.abstract: Mammalian biology unfolds over time, within tissues and organs opaque to our eyes and instruments. We applied DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, to record the cell lineage of a mouse over nearly two weeks of development. From one embryo, we reconstruct a time-calibrated, parsimony-supported, zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million transcriptionally profiled cells. A burst of editing unequivocally marks the daughters of the first cleavage, which serve as inline replicates. We quantify clonal dominance arising during gastrulation. Tree siblings share cell type far above chance; heterotypic siblings mark terminal differentiations. Temporal sweeps of clade co-occurrence recover a dated hierarchy of cell-type couplings; imputed labels for internal nodes recapitulate known state paths. A lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development, long out of reach, is coming into view.

items.title: Before the immunological Big Bang.
items.abstract: The nature of the gut microbiome before vaccination influences later inflammatory reactions and fever.

items.title: AI for research mathematics has arrived.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can now solve research problems in mathematics and verify the answers.

items.title: Hashimoto's thyroiditis: two decades on.
items.abstract: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is the most common cause of primary hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and is characterised by immune-mediated injury to thyroid follicular cells. Its pathophysiology involves an interplay of genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and epigenetic modifications that disrupt immune tolerance, promoting T-cell mediated thyroid injury and thyroid autoantibody production. The disease can progress from euthyroid autoimmunity to subclinical and overt hypothyroidism, with substantial variation in its course. Clinical manifestations vary with the extent of thyroid dysfunction and inflammatory activity. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, thyroid function testing, thyroid autoantibody measurement, and ultrasonography when indicated. Management centres on levothyroxine replacement for overt hypothyroidism, with an individualised approach to subclinical disease. Thyroidectomy is reserved for selected indications, whereas emerging immunomodulatory strategies remain investigational. This Review synthesises developments over the past two decades in the epidemiology, natural history, aetiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and management of Hashimoto's thyroiditis, and considers emerging mechanistic insights and approaches to precision medicine that might inform future disease-modifying therapies.

items.title: Hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among high-risk patients in India, 2023-25: a multicentre prospective study.

sections.objective: Melioidosis is not a nationally notifiable disease in India, and the absence of systematic surveillance has contributed to substantial under-recognition and fragmented epidemiological data. We aimed to determine the hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among hospitalised adults at high risk of melioidosis in India.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective, multicentre, hospital-based prevalence study between Jan 1, 2023, and Dec 31, 2025, across 15 tertiary care centres in India. Adults (aged ≥18 years) hospitalised with predefined community-acquired infectious syndromes and diabetes or chronic kidney disease were enrolled. Melioidosis was defined by culture confirmation. The primary outcome was hospital-based prevalence. Prespecified secondary analyses assessed geographical, syndrome-specific, and seasonal variation; factors associated with melioidosis; and clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes.
sections.results: Among 2953 patients, 262 (8·9% [95% CI 7·9-10·0]) had culture-confirmed melioidosis, with marked geographical heterogeneity. Prevalence was highest in Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka, and among patients presenting with extrapulmonary abscesses and bone and joint infections. Cases clustered during the monsoon months. Factors independently associated with melioidosis included monsoon admission (adjusted odds ratio 1·40 [95% CI 1·08-1·83]), male sex (2·33 [1·64-3·32]), outdoor high-risk occupation (1·94 [1·47-2·56]), and groundwater as the primary drinking-water source (3·25 [2·48-4·26]). Bacteraemia occurred in 152 (58%) of 262 patients with melioidosis, and 50 (19%) died in hospital.
sections.conclusion: Melioidosis is a frequent and severe infection among high-risk hospitalised adults in India, with substantial geographical variation and strong environmental and seasonal associations. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing and heightened clinical awareness among high-risk patients.

items.title: Incidence of clinically diagnosed infections in children with sickle cell anaemia treated with oral hydroxyurea in Angola, DR Congo, Kenya, and Uganda: a retrospective cohort study from the REACH trial.

sections.objective: Hydroxyurea is widely used in the first-line treatment of sickle cell anaemia; however, its mildly myelosuppressive effects when used at therapeutic doses have led to suggestions that treatment with hydroxyurea might increase the risk of infection. To address this question, we have investigated the incidence of clinically diagnosed infections among children within the Realizing Effectiveness Across Continents with Hydroxyurea (REACH) trial during various phases of hydroxyurea treatment.
sections.methods: REACH (NCT01966731 and NCT06171217) is an ongoing, phase 1/2, open-label, multicentre treatment trial of children with sickle cell anaemia with 2 months of screening followed by oral hydroxyurea at a fixed dose for 6 months and then dose escalation to the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). The current international, retrospective cohort study included children aged 1-10 years with sickle cell anaemia who were recruited and enrolled into REACH from four hospitals in Angola, DR Congo, Kenya, and Uganda and who had previously been followed up within the trial. Clinically diagnosed infections were characterised by likely aetiology and severity and incidence rate ratios (IRR) were then computed across time and during dosing phases as protocol-specified outcomes. The primary outcome of the current analysis was the incidence of clinically diagnosed infections, which was stratified by hydroxyurea treatment phase and assessed in all children who started fixed-dose hydroxyurea treatment. Rates of each clinically diagnosed infection (per 100 person-years of observation [PYO]) were calculated by age group and dosing phase.
sections.results: Between July 4, 2014, and Nov 11, 2016, 635 children were enrolled in the trial. 606 children (296 [49%] female and 310 [51%] male) completed screening and began treatment with hydroxyurea. Overall, 5493 infections occurred across 5638 PYO, with an incidence rate of 97·4/100 PYO. Among non-malarial infections, rates declined from the screening to fixed-dose phase (adjusted IRR 0·81 [95% CI 0·67-0·98]) and decreased further from the screening to the MTD phase (0·51 [0·43-0·61]; p<0·0001). Statistically significant decreases across the fixed-dose, dose-escalation, and MTD phases, respectively, were observed in the adjusted IRRs for upper respiratory tract infections (IRR 0·84 [95% CI 0·62-1·14], 0·77 [0·58-1·03], and 0·64 [0·47-0·88]; p=0·0051), lower respiratory tract infections (1·26 [0·69-2·31], 0·60 [0·32-1·12], and 0·45 [0·23-0·89]; p=0·021), bacterial skin or nail infections (0·58 [0·26-1·30], 0·32 [0·15-0·68], and 0·31 [0·14-0·66]; p=0·0025), and non-specific infectious syndromes (0·80 [0·58-1·11], 0·47 [0·35-0·63], and 0·39 [0·28-0·53]; p<0·0001). A similar decrease was observed for the adjusted IRR of grade 3 or higher infections across the fixed-dose, dose-escalation, and MTD phases, respectively (0·65 [0·42-1·00], 0·20 [0·13-0·32], and 0·48 [0·32-0·73]; p=0·0006).
sections.conclusion: In the large REACH cohort, the incidence rate or severity of clinically diagnosed infections in children with sickle cell anaemia living in sub-Saharan Africa, was not increased during the hydroxyurea treatment phases of this trial. Our results provide reassurance that, even when administered at MTD, hydroxyurea does not put children with sickle cell anaemia at increased risk of illness or death from infections. For the French, Portuguese and Swahili translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy for unresectable, homologous recombination deficiency-positive, high-grade serous ovarian cancer (NANT): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery is standard treatment for advanced ovarian cancer that is unlikely to achieve optimal cytoreduction. We aimed to evaluate a chemotherapy-free regimen of neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy in homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive disease initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery.
sections.methods: This single-arm, phase 2 trial was conducted at six tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, had treatment-naïve, FIGO stage III-IV HRD-positive high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer, an ECOG performance status of 0-2, with a low likelihood of complete primary debulking surgery based on prespecified criteria. Patients received oral niraparib monotherapy for two 28-day cycles with an individualised starting dose of 200 mg or 300 mg. Protocol-permitted supportive care was provided as clinically indicated. Co-primary endpoints were investigator-assessed objective response rate in the response-evaluable population and R0 resection rate after interval debulking surgery in the operated population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of niraparib. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04507841), is closed to enrolment, and this report presents the primary analysis.
sections.results: Between Jan 8, 2021, and Jul 18, 2023, 127 patients were screened, and 67 were enrolled into the study. All enrolled patients were female and self-identified as Han Chinese (median age 55 years [IQR 50-62]). At the data cutoff (Dec 29, 2025), median follow-up was 37·7 months (IQR 31·8-48·5). Among 48 response-evaluable patients, 30 achieved an objective response, with an objective response rate of 63% (95% CI 47-76). Among 40 operated patients, 32 achieved R0 resection, with an R0 resection rate of 80% (95% CI 64-91). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia in 32 (48%) of 67 patients, leukopenia in 13 (19%) patients, anaemia in 12 (18%) patients, and neutropenia in nine (13%) patients. Serious adverse events occurred in 19 (28%) patients. No treatment-related deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: Neoadjuvant niraparib showed anti-tumour activity and enabled R0 resection in selected patients with HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer who were initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery. This strategy remains investigational and requires randomised validation against standard platinum-taxane neoadjuvant chemotherapy. For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Migraine.
items.abstract: Migraine is a chronic neurovascular disorder characterised by recurrent attacks of moderate-to-severe head pain, accompanied by transient but disabling symptoms such as aura, nausea, vomiting, phonophobia, and photophobia, reflecting the involvement of multiple systems. Migraine affects and disables a large proportion of the global population. The pathogenesis of migraine involves the interplay of genetic and epigenetic factors across complex neurosensory and neurovascular networks. Decades of research have elucidated key components of these pathways, driving the development of mechanism-based therapies that are now transforming clinical practice and substantially improving patients' lives.

items.title: Evidence of artemisinin partial resistance in Zambia: a molecular epidemiology and clinical study.

sections.objective: Artemisinin derivatives are central to first-line treatment of both uncomplicated and severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Emerging artemisinin partial resistance in east Africa threatens to spread across the continent.
sections.methods: In two cross-sectional studies conducted across the ten provinces of Zambia in 2024, we genotyped the artemisinin resistance-associated gene Pfkelch13. Children aged 6-72 months were recruited from randomly selected households in the first study, and patients 6 months or older presenting with malarial symptoms at 100 selected health facilities were recruited in the second study. In Kaoma, western Zambia, we recruited patients aged 12 months or older with microscopically confirmed P falciparum infection and a positive rapid diagnostic test. We evaluated the association between Pfkelch13 genotype and day 3 parasite positivity following treatment with artemisinin-based combination therapy, as well as ex-vivo parasite susceptibility to dihydroartemisinin (the active metabolite of artemisinin). We also assessed longitudinal changes in Pfkelch13 mutation prevalence in Kaoma using isolates collected during therapeutic efficacy studies and community surveys conducted from 2018 to 2026.
sections.results: We identified a novel mutation, Pfkelch13 A724E, in 113 (52%) of 217 isolates (95% CI 45-59) from Western Province, 94 (51%) of 184 isolates (95% CI 44-59) from North-Western Province, and 229 (11·7%) of 1949 isolates countrywide. In Kaoma, 28% (21 of 75 [95% CI 18-40]) of patients carrying Pfkelch13 A724E mutant parasites before treatment were parasite-positive on day 3, compared with 0% (zero of 23; [0-15]) of patients with the wild-type allele (p=0·0026). Within the patients who were positive at day 3, the proportion of A724E mutant parasites increased significantly after treatment (p=0·0039). The prevalence of Pfkelch13 A724E in Kaoma increased steadily from 0% (0 of 15 isolates [95% CI 0-22]) in 2018 to 79% (132 of 167 [73-85]) in 2026. No significant ex-vivo growth inhibition was observed in Pfkelch13 A724E parasites after dihydroartemisinin exposure.
sections.conclusion: A novel Pfkelch13 mutation clinically associated with partial resistance to artemisinin is spreading in Zambia. Additional clinical evaluations are urgently needed in the region.

items.title: Regional expansion and adaptive evolution of multidrug-resistant Candida tropicalis in China: a retrospective, multicentre, genomic study.

sections.objective: The emergence of antifungal-resistant Candida tropicalis poses a severe threat to human health and complicates clinical management, yet the molecular epidemiology and mechanisms underlying its resistance and persistence in hospital settings remain poorly understood. We aimed to investigate the regional epidemiology, persistence and virulence trade-offs, and adaptive traits associated with the expansion of multidrug-resistant C tropicalis.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective, multicentre, genomic study of C tropicalis isolates from 84 hospitals in east China and included additional multidrug-resistant (resistant to azoles and echinocandins) isolates from active surveillance at Shanghai East Hospital. We analysed clinical metadata from this hospital to identify risk factors for multidrug-resistant isolate recovery and 30-day mortality. We conducted whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, phenotypic assays, and experimental evolution to elucidate resistance mechanisms, virulence dynamics, and adaptive traits.
sections.results: 1184 clinical isolates from Jan 1, 2017, to Dec 31, 2024, were included; of these, 356 (30·1%) were azole resistant and 98 (8·3%) were multidrug resistant. We identified the regional expansion of a multidrug-resistant C tropicalis lineage, DST849, which accounted for 92 (94%) of 98 multidrug-resistant cases and was predominantly isolated from the urinary tract. Admission to a surgical ward (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 46·37, 95% CI 17·48-123·00) and intubation (32·30, 10·28-101·45) were key risk factors for multidrug-resistant isolate recovery. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that multidrug-resistant C tropicalis isolation was an independent predictor of 30-day mortality (aOR 2·84, 95% CI 1·31-6·16; p=0·0081). Phylogenomic analysis revealed that multidrug-resistant isolates evolved from azole-resistant ancestors (DST225) via the acquisition of FKS1 mutations (S30P) while retaining ERG11 mutations (Y132F and S154F) and acquired a distinguishing ICL1 (Y43T) loss-of-heterozygosity mutation.
sections.conclusion: Our findings reveal the emergence of multidrug-resistant Ctropicalis through lineage-specific expansion, driven by genetic plasticity and adaptive stress responses. These adaptations might facilitate persistence under antifungal and environmental pressures in health-care settings. These insights underscore the urgent need for improved antifungal stewardship, targeted genomic surveillance, and interventions to mitigate multidrug-resistant fungal threats.

items.title: Epidemiological trends of HIV among individuals aged 15-54 years in South Africa from 2004 to 2025: a population-based, longitudinal cohort study.

sections.objective: South Africa has mounted the largest HIV prevention and treatment programme in history, delivering substantial gains in survival and prevention of new HIV infections; however, service disruptions and recent funding losses might jeopardise these successes. There is a scarcity of high-quality, population-based empirical evidence on key epidemic metrics needed to accurately gauge recent progress towards epidemic control in South Africa. We aimed to evaluate recent progress towards HIV epidemic control in South Africa by quantifying long-term trends in key epidemic control metrics in a large population-based cohort in rural KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
sections.methods: In this population-based, longitudinal cohort study, we used prospectively collected HIV testing, sociodemographic, behavioural, and population viral load data from the Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) health and demographic surveillance system in rural KwaZulu-Natal from 2003 to 2025. Population-based HIV surveys (encompassing individual health interview and HIV testing) take place annually in all consenting resident individuals aged 15 years or older. We used Poisson regression models to quantify trends in directly observed HIV incidence in repeat testers (aged 15-54 years) who had initially tested negative for HIV and subsequently received at least one valid HIV test result. We further analysed 11 rounds of population viral load testing conducted between 2011 and 2025. We used generalised estimating equations to quantify population viral suppression metrics and calculated trends in the incidence-to-prevalence ratio, a key metric for evaluating progress towards epidemic control.
sections.results: Between June 24, 2003, and May 22, 2025, across the population cohort, 59 806 (65·4%) of 91 367 contacted individuals aged 15-54 years consented to participate at least once in population-based HIV testing. Of those tested, 33 754 (56·4%) were female and 26 052 (43·6%) were male, with a median age of 26·7 years (IQR 19·3-39·1) at testing date. Among 42 662 participants who initially tested HIV negative and were recontacted, 29 702 (69·6%) underwent repeat HIV testing and were included in the incidence analysis. In this group, over 182 112 person-years of observation, we observed 4852 HIV seroconversions. From 2013 to 2018, overall annual HIV incidence rates declined by 52·2% in males and 36·9% in females. We found no evidence of a continued downward trend in HIV incidence between 2019 and 2025 among either females or males. After a period of substantial decline (from 2011 to 2018), population detectable viraemia increased significantly from 2019 to 2025 by 9·6 percentage points (95% CI 5·4-13·8), remaining an estimated 30·7 percentage points (95% CI 27·2-34·3) below the UNAIDS 95-95-95 population viral suppression target. The incidence-to-prevalence ratio decreased substantially across consecutive survey rounds, from 0·132 (95% CI 0·114-0·152) in 2006 to its lowest recorded value of 0·034 (95% CI 0·028-0·042) in 2022, representing an overall 74·2% decline. After 2022, the ratio stagnated above the epidemic control benchmark of 0·03.
sections.conclusion: These epidemic metrics show that progress towards HIV epidemic control is faltering in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The tools to reverse this trajectory are available; the challenge now is to ensure their sustained and effective implementation through coordinated action across research, policy, government, civil society, and international funding partners. We can, and we should, change course now if we want to achieve an AIDS-free generation in South Africa and the world.

items.title: Management of Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Routine US Clinical Practice: Impact of Delayed Treatment Initiation.

sections.objective: To understand management of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in routine US clinical practice to identify gaps in patient care.
sections.methods: Retrospective analysis of electronic medical records from the Vestrum database. Treatment-naive eyes newly diagnosed with nAMD from January 1, 2014, with ≥1-years' follow-up. Cumulative incidence of eyes receiving treatment was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier, and factors predicting anti-VEGF receipt through 1 year were evaluated by logistic regression. Proportion of eyes treated over 3 years, baseline factors associated with receiving treatment within 1 year of diagnosis and with delayed (3-12 months after diagnosis) versus prompt (within 29 days of diagnosis) treatment initiation.
sections.results: Of 90 681 eyes included in the analysis, 23% did not receive anti-VEGF treatment at diagnosis, declining to 16%, 15%, and 13% at years 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Mean baseline VA of eyes not treated and treated was 39 and 52 letters, respectively. Eyes were more likely to receive treatment (odds ratio [OR] ≥ 1.50, [95% CI]) if they had baseline VA 20/40-20/100 versus ≥ 20/40 (1.52 [1.44, 1.61]), macular edema (3.26 [3.11, 3.42]), subretinal fluid (4.97 [4.75, 5.20]), or subretinal pigment epithelium fluid (1.64 [1.56, 1.72]). Eyes were less likely to receive treatment (OR ≤ 0.50) if they had simultaneous bilateral diagnosis of nAMD vs. unilateral diagnosis (0.32 [0.31, 0.34]), or baseline VA 9 injections, respectively. In eyes that received >9 injections, those with baseline VA < 20/400 gained 27.2 letters.
sections.conclusion: Overall, approximately one-quarter of eyes with nAMD were not treated within 29 days of diagnosis. Simultaneous bilateral nAMD diagnosis and poor baseline VA (< 20/400) were primary factors associated with not receiving anti-VEGF treatment. Greater VA gains were observed with prompt treatment and increasing number of injections.

items.title: Twelve-Month Results of Cyanoacrylate Closure in Patients with Venous Leg Ulceration.

sections.objective: Venous leg ulceration (VLU) is a major cause of patient distress and healthcare burden. Previous studies have highlighted the importance of early endovenous ablation of superficial venous reflux to expedite healing and prevent recurrence, but the optimal venous ablation modality is unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of cyanoacrylate closure in patients with VLU.
sections.methods: A global, prospective, single-arm observational study was conducted in 17 centers across the United States and Europe. A total of 125 participants with VLU were included and treated with the VenaSeal closure system, in addition to standard wound therapy, including multilayered compression. Adjuvant treatments to varicosities, perforators or the sub-ulcer plexus were left to the discretion of treating clinicians. The primary outcome was VLU healing through 12 months. Secondary outcomes included time to ulcer recurrence, anatomic vein closure, target limb adverse events, and changes in quality-of-life measures.
sections.results: One hundred twenty-five participants with VLU and saphenous vein reflux were enrolled. The mean (± standard deviation) age was 67.9 ± 14.76 years, with 38.4% females and an overall mean BMI of 32.4± 9.35. Concomitant foam sclerotherapy treatments were performed in 19.7% (31/157) of target veins. At 12 months, ulcer healing was 81.3% and ulcer recurrence was 17.0%. The median time to ulcer healing was 92 days (95% CI 74, 137). Anatomic vein closure was successful in 82.7% of all target veins. CEC-adjudicated AE and SAEs included: 2 granulomas, 1 hypersensitivity reaction, and 4 cases of phlebitis of the treated limb. Healthcare services utilized outside of the index procedure yielded 0.12 adjunctive therapies per vein-year. Venous-specific and generic QoL scores showed sustained improvement compared to baseline scores.
